# Diagnostic Tool Design — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Diagnostic Tool Design. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Offline analysis is one way to avoid issuing additional database commands during diagnosis: the mdbkit repository describes analysis commands that read supplied files without a database connection and print proposed actions for human review. This is a documented architectural example, not an independent audit of the implementation or a claim that every diagnostic task can be completed offline. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/saqibameen86/mdbkit

## How it works

- [statement] Production diagnostic collectors should expose scope and deadline controls. Percona mongodb_exporter documents collection allowlists, a collection-count threshold that disables selected collectors, and a timeout offset; it warns that free-space statistics can cause delays with many collections or indexes. This supports bounding collection work, without proving that every diagnostic command is lock-free. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/percona/mongodb_exporter/blob/main/REFERENCE.md
- [statement] The mdiag _redactfile function matches a finite list of configuration secret names, substitutes a redacted marker, and includes a SHA-256 digest when available. This is targeted redaction, not evidence of general query-document PII coverage. OWASP recommends removing or protecting sensitive log data through several possible methods; it does not mandate regex redaction as the sole compliant design. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://example.test/withheld-reference · keywords: Diagnostic Tool Design · also: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] MongoDB ftdc NewStreamingCollector bounds retained batches by sample count: Add flushes when count reaches maxSamples, and FlushCollector resolves the payload, writes it, and resets the collector. This is a collection-side sample limit; the implementation does not establish a strict byte-buffer cap for a streaming BSON parser or prove prevention of replica-node OOM kills. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/ftdc/blob/main/collector_streaming.go
- [statement] A diagnostic bundle needs redaction coverage appropriate to its contents. The mdiag _redactfile implementation matches an explicit list of configuration-secret keys, while independent diagnosis-data research explains that rule and regex approaches can both miss sensitive data and remove useful evidence. Inference: the presence of a regex redactor alone cannot establish complete PII protection. (medium confidence) — https://example.test/withheld-reference · keywords: Diagnostic Tool Design · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2409.17535v1
- [statement] Query shapes can group similar queries without distinguishing every literal value: MongoDB examples use different date constants with the same shape hashes. Namespace and field-name protection is a separate concern: $queryStats offers transformIdentifiers for hashing those identifiers. Inference: shape-based grouping should not be presented as complete anonymization or as proof of deterministic error grouping. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md · keywords: Diagnostic Tool Design · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [statement] MongoDB documents query shapes as a way to group similar queries, including examples where different date constants yield the same shape hash. This supports grouping query workloads, but not guaranteed deterministic error grouping or anonymization: Atlas explicitly warns that shapes retaining field names can contain PII even when values are redacted. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md · keywords: Diagnostic Tool Design · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md
- [statement] serverStatus exposes separate lock-wait counters and election-reason counters, including elections after a member cannot reach its primary within electionTimeoutMillis. These counters can inform a diagnostic tool's evidence model; the command reference does not establish that a scraper timeout held a database lock and caused an election, or that a small serverStatus timeout fixes that sequence. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Collector scope is a concrete overhead control: Percona's exporter reference provides collection filters and a collection-count cutoff for selected collectors, and warns that free-space statistics can delay processing with many collections or indexes. PMM documentation likewise warns that high collection limits can increase CPU and memory use. Design inference: expose selective collection rather than assuming all diagnostic commands are cheap. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/percona/mongodb_exporter/blob/main/REFERENCE.md · keywords: Diagnostic Tool Design · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/use/commands/pmm-admin/add.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The inspected implementations distinguish retention control from input validation: MongoDB's streaming collector flushes and resets after a sample-count threshold, while js-bson checks declared document lengths against the supplied buffer and checks document termination. These passages support testing both controls separately; they do not establish a strict parser byte cap or prove prevention of replica-node OOM kills. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/ftdc/blob/main/collector_streaming.go · keywords: Diagnostic Tool Design · also: https://github.com/mongodb/js-bson/blob/main/src/parser/deserializer.ts
